summary: Develop practical gender-responsive M&E skills for social protection programmes. Build indicators, dashboards, evaluation plans, and action reports. Enrol today
lede: Gender-responsive monitoring and evaluation for social protection uses gender analysis and programme evidence to assess who benefits and who remains excluded. For intermediate practitioners, programme officers, gender advisers and policy analysts, the course addresses how to improve evidence for programme decisions. Participants practise designing disaggregated indicators, assessing social registry data quality and using beneficiary feedback in evaluation and reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who monitor, evaluate, fund, manage, or improve social protection policies and programmes. It suits intermediate practitioners who already work with programme data or results frameworks and need to integrate gender analysis into routine monitoring and evaluation. A social protection M&E officer can use the course to strengthen indicators and reporting, while a gender adviser can translate analysis into programme decisions.
modules: Theory of Change and Results Frameworks
prerequisites: You should have practical experience in monitoring, evaluation, social protection programming, gender analysis, policy analysis, or programme reporting. You should be comfortable reading a results framework and working with basic tables or spreadsheets. No coding or programming is required. Advanced digital analytics and AI-assisted qualitative coding are introduced at operational application level, not technical engineering level.
